title: Cube shaped filters. Cylinder shaped socket.
description:
Cube shaped filters. Cylinder shaped socket. The command module used cubic lithium hydroxide canisters to scrub carbon dioxide. The lunar module used cylindrical ones and had no backups, says Space Center Houston.

The lander was built for two people. HobbySpace says it was designed for two people for 36 hours, not three people for 96.

About 1am, four hours after the explosion. Crew systems chief Ed Smylie realised then that carbon dioxide had to be dealt with, according to collectSPACE via Space.com.

Chief of NASA's crew systems division. He said probably 60 people were involved.

A hose, a sock, a plastic bag, cue cards and duct tape. That is the Space.com list. HobbySpace adds a flight manual cover. Accounts differ on the exact parts.

The crew called it the mail box. NASA's caption reads: Apollo 13 Crew Installing 'Mail Box' for Purging Carbon Dioxide From Lunar Module, April 14, 1970.

Houston could not send pictures. It talked the crew through it.

Sources:
- https://spacecenter.org/apollo-13-infographic-how-did-they-make-that-co2-scrubber/: read in full. Established that the command module used cubic lithium hydroxide scrubbers and the lunar module cylindric ones, that the crew had plenty for the command module but no backups for the lunar module, and that Mission Control could not send pictures and described everything verbally.
- https://www.space.com/space-exploration/apollo/nasa-engineer-ed-smylie-who-led-carbon-dioxide-fix-on-apollo-13-dies-at-95: read in full (collectSPACE report, 29 April 2025). Established Ed Smylie as chief of NASA's crew systems division, that he realised at about one in the morning, four hours after the explosion, that carbon dioxide had to be dealt with, his statement that probably 60 people were involved, and the materials: a spacesuit hose, a sock, a plastic bag, cue cards and duct tape.
- https://hobbyspace.com/Blog/?p=8241: read in full. Established that the lunar module was built for two people for 36 hours rather than three for 96, the materials including a flight manual cover, suit parts and socks, and the crew's name for the rig, mailbox. A repost of a Gizmodo article, so not independent.
- https://www.nasa.gov/history/afj/ap13fj/: read the landing page. Established NASA's image caption: Apollo 13 Crew Installing 'Mail Box' for Purging Carbon Dioxide From Lunar Module, April 14, 1970.
